source.title: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training
source.authors: Jing-Yuan Liu; Jianling Su; Xingcheng Yao; Zhe-Jun Jiang; Guokun Lai; Yulun Du; Yidao Qin; Wei-Xin Xu; Enzhe Lu; Junjie Yan; Yan-Ru Chen; Hua-Bin Zheng; Yi-Bo Liu; Shao-Wei Liu; Bo-Hong Yin; Wei-Ran He; Han Zhu; Yu-Zhi Wang; Jian-Zhou Wang; Meng Dong; Zheng Zhang; Yong-Sheng Kang; Hao Zhang; Xin-Ran Xu; Yu-Tao Zhang; Yu-Xin Wu; Xin-Yu Zhou; Zhi-Lin Yang

record.tranche_reason: The study runs its own scaling-law experiments, fitting language-model loss against compute and estimating compute-optimal model and token scaling; it uses its own optimizer comparison and training setup rather than reproducing the original studies exactly.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the fitted loss-versus-compute curves and the reported AdamW compute-optimal parameter/token relationships. Downstream benchmark comparisons, SFT results, and spectral-entropy measurements do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Mainly an optimizer paper that uses scaling-law fits to compare Muon with AdamW. Its one independent result on a version is the AdamW baseline allocation search (Appendix B, Table 9). Model size N is varied at fixed FLOPs under C=6ND, Pareto-optimal N–D pairs are picked by validation loss, and N(C) and D(C) power laws are fitted. That is a Chinchilla-style test of V3 in a new setup (proprietary data, 8K context, Llama dense). The loss-versus-compute curves (Table 3) impose a power-law form to compare optimizers. They report no fit quality, so they do not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that weight decay and per-matrix update-RMS scaling let Muon scale. Scaling-law fits show about 2× compute efficiency over AdamW (about 52% of FLOPs). Muon can replace AdamW for large-scale LLM training, as shown by the 3B/16B MoE Moonlight.
record.recipe_differences: Uses power-law fitting and compute-constrained scaling experiments, but compares Muon and AdamW in the authors’ own Llama-architecture runs and proprietary-data setup rather than reproducing the original studies’ full experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted loss-versus-compute exponent differs slightly between the Muon and AdamW runs. The reported compute-optimal allocation fits are for AdamW only.

fits_no_version.finding: Muon's fitted loss-versus-compute curve sits below AdamW's (prefactor 2.506 vs 2.608). Muon needs about 52% of AdamW FLOPs for equal loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice shifts the loss-compute scaling curve by a roughly constant compute multiplier without changing the exponent much.

record.problems: The loss-fit series covers a limited model-size range (399M–1.5B parameters); the data are proprietary; no uncertainty estimates for the fitted curves or exponents are reported. The compute-optimal allocation fit is reported for AdamW, not as a separate Muon allocation fit.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream benchmark scores, SFT comparisons, weight-growth measurements, and SVD-entropy results were left out because they do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Whether loss actually follows a power law: no fit-quality evidence, and no separate scaling in parameters or tokens.
All; shape varies with size in Table 2 and is not controlled at fixed parameter count.
All; benchmarks are not related to scale or loss.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter counting, schedules or data. Optimizer dependence of the exponent is not assessable without uncertainty. Curve bending is not examined.

missing.what: IsoFLOP loss bowls (loss vs train tokens, learning rate and batch size at about 1e20–1.1e21 FLOPs), showing distinct minima behind the N(C) and D(C) fits

record.verdict_notes: Treat this as a weak, incidental test. The scaling laws are mainly a measuring tool for an optimizer comparison, and the V3 evidence comes from hyperparameter tuning of the baseline. The reader's V1 and V7 'supports' labels are removed. For V1 the power-law form is imposed without fit diagnostics. For V7 the 0.002 exponent difference has no uncertainty and involves only one setup change. The Muon runs reuse AdamW's compute-optimal allocation, so no Muon allocation is fitted.

versions.untested_parts: The reported loss fits are against compute in compute-optimal runs; parameter-only and token-only loss scaling with the other quantities not bottlenecking is not separately tested.
No held-out test of predictions from small runs against runs orders of magnitude larger is reported.

The reported parameter/token allocation relationships are for the AdamW baseline. The study does not separately fit a compute-optimal allocation for Muon, nor test allocation across different data, schedules, or fitting procedures.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or training regimes are tested for the same power-law form.
Downstream benchmarks are reported, but the study does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.

The fitted loss-versus-compute exponents are reported for two optimizers, but other setup and fitting choices, disagreement across published laws, and bending away from a single power law are not tested.

rows.subject: Muon scaling-law model series (Llama architecture)
rows.operation_detail: Fit LM loss against training compute in scaling-law experiments.

conditions.value: compute-optimal training; Muon reuses AdamW-optimal hyperparameters

rows.note: The table reports the fitted loss curve; the figure compares it with the AdamW fit.
rows.check: This is the study's own method (Muon) set against its baseline. The power-law form is imposed for the comparison, with no residuals or goodness-of-fit, and Muon reuses AdamW's N/D/hyperparameters. It does not bear on V1. For V7 the exponent gap (0.052 vs 0.054) has no uncertainty, so it cannot be read as a real setup dependence.

rows.subject: AdamW scaling-law model series (Llama architecture)
rows.operation_detail: Fit LM loss against training compute in scaling-law experiments.
rows.note: The fitted exponent differs slightly from the Muon fit in r1.
rows.check: AdamW fit spanning about 1e-2 to 1e1 PFLOP/s-days (Figure 3). The form is assumed, and no fit quality or deviation from the power law is reported, so it cannot confirm V1. Delinked from V7: one setup cannot show fit-dependence, and the gap to Muon has no uncertainty.

rows.subject: AdamW baseline scaling-law runs
rows.operation_detail: Search compute-constrained model-size and token-count combinations, then fit empirical relationships with compute.
rows.measure: Compute-optimal parameter count N as a function of FLOPs C
rows.locator: Appendix B, Table 9; search procedure in Appendix B
rows.note: The study says it searches N and D under fixed compute and records validation loss to select Pareto-optimal combinations.
rows.check: Value correct. The isoFLOP search spans only about 1e20–1.1e21 FLOPs (Figure 5), roughly one order of magnitude, and no uncertainty is given. The exponent 0.511 sits close to Hoffmann's equal scaling.

rows.subject: AdamW baseline scaling-law runs
rows.operation_detail: Search compute-constrained model-size and token-count combinations, then fit empirical relationships with compute.
rows.measure: Compute-optimal training token count D as a function of FLOPs C
rows.locator: Appendix B, Table 9; search procedure in Appendix B
rows.note: The fitted token exponent is close to the fitted parameter-count exponent in r3.
rows.check: Value correct. D exponent 0.489 makes N and D grow roughly equally. Same narrow compute range and no uncertainty as r3.

relationships.condition: AdamW dense Llama models, proprietary data, 8K context, isoFLOP budgets about 1e20–1e21 FLOPs
relationships.reason: The fitted compute-optimal N∝C^0.511 and D∝C^0.489 each grow as a power of compute, about equally as Hoffmann et al. find (r3, r4). The compute range is narrow and no uncertainty is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Fitted optimal parameter and token exponents were 0.511 and 0.489 over a narrow compute range, without reported uncertainty.
